question: Which year marks two decades since the launch of the ASHA programme?
solution:
The correct answer is __**2025**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **ASHA programme** (Accredited Social Health Activist) was launched by the Government of India in **2005** under the **National Rural Health Mission (NRHM)**.
 
• The programme was designed to provide **community health workers** to improve healthcare delivery and outcomes in rural areas.
 
• The year **2025** marks **two decades (20 years)** since its inception in **2005**, making it a significant milestone for this initiative.
 
• **ASHA workers** act as the primary interface between the community and the healthcare system, focusing on maternal and child health, immunizations, and preventive healthcare.
 
• Over the years, the programme has been widely recognized for its role in improving health indicators such as **infant mortality rate (IMR)** and **maternal mortality rate (MMR)**, especially in rural India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **National Rural Health Mission (NRHM):**

 
 
• Launched in **2005** by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, the NRHM aimed to provide accessible, affordable, and quality healthcare to rural populations.
 
• The programme focused on strengthening healthcare infrastructure, improving human resources, and addressing inequities in healthcare delivery.
 
• ASHA workers were introduced under NRHM to act as the link between the community and the healthcare system.
 
 
 
• **Role of ASHA Workers:**
 
 
• ASHA workers are primarily women from the local community who promote health awareness and encourage utilization of healthcare services.
 
• They are involved in activities such as **promoting institutional deliveries, immunizations, sanitation practices, and nutrition awareness**.
 
• They also act as facilitators for accessing government health schemes and benefits.
 
 
 
• **Impact of the ASHA Programme:**
 
 
• The programme has contributed significantly to improved health outcomes in rural areas, especially in reducing **maternal and infant mortality rates**.
 
• ASHA workers have played an important role in **mobilizing communities** during health campaigns such as polio eradication and the COVID-19 vaccination drive.
 
 
 
• **Global Recognition:**
 
 
• The ASHA programme has been praised internationally for its innovative approach to addressing rural healthcare challenges.
 
• It serves as a model for community health programmes in other developing countries.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **ASHA Workers’ Training:**

 
 
• ASHA workers undergo **continuous training** to ensure they are equipped with the latest knowledge and skills.
 
• Training modules include topics like **maternal and child health, communicable diseases, and non-communicable diseases**.
 
 
 
• **Challenges Faced by ASHA Workers:**
 
 
• Despite their critical role, ASHA workers often face challenges such as **low remuneration, lack of resources, and difficult working conditions**.
 
• Efforts are being made to address these issues through policy interventions and additional incentives.
 
 
 
• **Future Goals:**
 
 
• The Government aims to expand the scope of the ASHA programme to include urban areas under the **National Urban Health Mission (NUHM)**.
 
• Focus remains on strengthening healthcare delivery systems, especially in under-served and remote regions.
